en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 24.9.
Hetuduka, Piṭṭhiduka

Conditioned by a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by insight, a state that is a root and to be abandoned by insight arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root [condition] there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by insight, a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by insight arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root there are three; under predominance there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance there are three.

Conditioned by a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by cultivation, a state that is a root and to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by cultivation, a state that is neither a root nor to be abandoned by cultivation arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root, three under predominance; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a non-root phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by vision, a non-root phenomenon whose root is to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] under root; ... pe ... one under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a non-root phenomenon whose root is not to be abandoned by vision, a non-root phenomenon whose root is not to be abandoned by vision arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Three under root; three under object; ... pe ... three under conascence.
Five ... [and so on] ... five in non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause and has a root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state that is a root-cause and has a root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. One in root; ... [and so on] ... one in non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause and does not have a root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation, there arises a state that is not a root-cause and does not have a root-cause to be abandoned by cultivation.
A state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: three … pe … under conascence:
five … pe … under non-disappearance: five.
Dependent on a state that is not a root and without applied thought, a state that is a root and with applied thought arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to the root condition (*hetu*), three; ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance (*avigata*), three. (Abbreviated in all cases.

Conditioned by a state that is neither-root nor with-conflict (*na-hetu na-saraṇa*), a state that is root and with-conflict (*hetu saraṇa*) arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. With respect to the root condition, three; ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, three.

Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor without-conflict (*na-hetu na-araṇa*), a state that is neither-root and without-conflict (*na-hetu araṇa*) arises by way of the root condition. [Dependent on] a state that is not-root (*nanahetu*)...
Dependent on a non-conflict state that is not a root-cause, a non-conflict state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is both not a root-cause and not a conflict, and dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor a conflict, a non-conflict state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three;
under predominance-condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance-condition there are three.
